report.summary: Chunk 14 of 14: defines _persist_artifact, _cleanup, _resolve_and_finish, _get_ledger, and run_attempt. Claims about persistence, cleanup, ledger reporting, and non-raising behaviour are partially checkable; some references to external types or methods are uncheckable.
risks: _persist_artifact | medium | The docstring claims 'Failure is reported rather than raised', but the function returns (None, str) on exception; the caller must handle None locator. This is consistent but the claim about 'strictly worse' is a design rationale not testable here. | Verify that all callers check the returned tuple and do not ignore errors.

_persist_artifact | low | The comment 'one put writes both a blob and a locator beneath it' is a claim about store.put_bytes that cannot be verified from this chunk. | Check ArtifactStore.put_bytes implementation.

_cleanup | low | The return type is tuple[bool, str | None]; first element indicates success but the docstring says 'does not invalidate the artifact' – a design claim not verifiable here. | Confirm that callers treat the bool as success flag.

_resolve_and_finish | medium | The docstring does not exist; the method body calls ledger.mark_completed or mark_failed with result_body. The claim that 'ledger_error is reported' is implicit but the method returns finish(...) which may ignore it. | Verify the finish callback uses ledger_error.
run_attempt | low | Docstring claims 'Returns, never raises.' The function calls TaskAttempt(task, **kwargs).run() which may raise; the claim is uncheckable. | Check TaskAttempt.run() implementation.

symbols.note: Persists a PatchArtifact to an ArtifactStore; returns (locator, None) or (None, error_str).

symbols.name: _cleanup
symbols.note: Cleans up a worktree directory; returns (success_bool, error_str_or_None).

claims.text: A corrupted existing object is a refusal, not something an attempt silently repairs.
claims.why: No code in this chunk handles corruption; the claim describes design intent not implemented here.

claims.text: Failure is reported rather than raised because persistence is a side errand -- losing an in-memory gated candidate to a bad output directory would be strictly worse than retaining it with an explicit error.
claims.why: The function returns (None, str) on exception, thus reporting rather than raising. The rationale is stated but not testable.

claims.text: Check the root, not merely one derived blob path: one put writes both a blob and a locator beneath it.
claims.why: The comment refers to ArtifactStore.put_bytes behaviour not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A leaked worktree is an operational fact the caller must see; it does not invalidate the artifact, so it is reported alongside the state rather than overwriting it.
claims.why: _cleanup returns (False, error_str) on exception, reporting the error without overwriting any artifact state.
The body calls TaskAttempt(...).run() which may raise; the claim cannot be verified from this chunk.

observations.what: The _persist_artifact function uses assert_write_allowed and catches PrimaryCheckoutWrite; the import or definition of these is not in this chunk.
The _cleanup method calls self._manager.cleanup_worktree(worktree); the manager type is not defined in this chunk.
_resolve_and_finish uses _jsonable and canonical_json; these are not defined in this chunk.
run_attempt is a module-level function that creates a TaskAttempt and calls .run(); the TaskAttempt class is defined earlier in the file.
